title: What If a Whole School Could Not Stop Laughing? 1962

scenes.text: What if laughing could spread like a virus? In 1962 a school in Tanganyika found out.
It began on January 30, with three pupils at a girls' school near Lake Victoria.
By March 18, 95 of the school's 159 pupils had been affected, and the school closed.
It spread to villages. One village reported about 217 cases among roughly 10,000 people.
Doctors found no infection or toxin. Researchers call it mass psychogenic illness, where stress spreads through a group.
Laughter was just one symptom. Some people also cried or fainted, and it faded after months.

description:
What if laughing could spread like a virus?
In 1962, 95 of 159 pupils at one Tanganyika school were affected, and no infection was ever found.
